text.p: GeneMedicine Inc said Tuesday it has received a $1.25 million quarterly research and development payment from Corange Ltd, the parent company of Boehringer Mannheim.
The payment is part of a 1995 collaborative alliance agreement for GeneMedicine and Boehringer Mannheim to develop gene medicines for the treatment of head and neck cancer and melanoma.

GeneMedicine said it expects Phase I human clinical trials for its IL-2 Gene Medicine, which is to be used to treat head and neck cancer, will begin in the next several weeks. The IL-2 treatment is the first to be developed under the alliance.
Under the alliance, Corange makes quarterly payments of $1.25 million to GeneMedicine and makes annual equity investments of $4 million.
So far, Corange has made payments totaling $13.35 million in research and development funding, and $12 million in equity investments.
A GeneMedicine spokeswoman said Corange is based in Bermuda.
